rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
Ritual / practice (noun) / ceremony — hard ban
No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
Register match.
Rough-cut drafts for articles.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Module file, not article draft.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Practitioners mentioned in pre-reads section (Horthy, Cherny) with credit; Klaassen attribution in maintainer block per maintainer's strategy-tying note; no paraphrase of technique in body without credit.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "We are all learners" in room-agreement section is in-scope carve-out per pedagogy §27 accept-note; no "the student" found; "you" used throughout operationally.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Terms like "agent's self-report", "scrollback", "loop" are either earned in body or appear in Key Concepts (structural signposting section exempt); no maintainer-only vocabulary leaked.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No reassurance-shaped hedges detected (no phrases like "no penalty", "it's OK if", "not a downgrade").

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No reference artifacts with framing sections in this module file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cap practitioner attribution at one student-side mention per module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Two different practitioners mentioned (Dex Horthy once, Boris Cherny once) in pre-reads; each mentioned once; no same-practitioner repetition; different practitioners do not trigger cap.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Module file structure not employing punchy framings requiring carve-outs.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No positioning defense phrases ("not aspirational", "not vendor", "grounded in actual", "from the person running it") detected in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Terms used (agent, skill, subagent, loop, tracker) appear in structural/operational contexts where they're either explained or appropriately scoped; no premature jargon planting.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Section closers point forward (to Module 2, exercises); no dangling pronouns or bypass-the-agent punchlines.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Standard shape for the `**What happened:**` block
rules_evaluated.evidence: Module file; rule applies to exercise recap sections.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No combative verbs (bark, order, command, whip, force, etc.) found describing student-agent interaction.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All section headers (Getting going + context, Big Idea, Prework, What You'll Learn, How we work, Start here, Key Concepts, Next, Pre-reads) are literally accurate.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No empty negations, deictic drumroll, bold-label echo, or citation duplication detected.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Big Idea and Key Concepts name positive capabilities (run loop, introspect, fix, close, compound); no corrective-gap framing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 3: `> Run M1 on `high` thinking effort (the training default).` HARM: in the first module, the bare abbreviation asks a new reader to decode a curriculum convention before Module 2 establishes it; that small decode cost arrives at the operational opening. The harm is present. The rule's M1 boundary explicitly requires the full form here.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Spell out `Module 1` in the opening reminder.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule applies to Agents 101; this is AE101 (student audience = engineers, not business executives).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Memory vs context — use deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Context is explained on line 57 as what fills the session window; no memory/context confusion is present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION; read to the boundary before cutting anything.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body describes golden path (exercises to run); recovery/troubleshooting moves routed to maintainer section below fence; time-critical rescues (if any) would be placed in body per carve-out.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lines 31 and 77: `All modules are designed to cope with missing details from prior modules` and `The instinct earns itself in use.` HARM: both forward-looking closes make the curriculum or an abstraction the actor, so the reader must translate a course claim into their own next move; the harm is present. No maintainer accept-note protects either phrasing.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Close each forward callout with the reader as actor, while preserving the permission to continue with missing details.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
